questions.question: How do combinations and permutations differ?

Combinations ignore order, while permutations count order
Combinations apply only to probabilities, while permutations apply only to events
questions.explanation: A combination selects a subset (order irrelevant), whereas a permutation arranges elements (order significant), so the same selection can correspond to many permutations.

option_explanations: This is reversed: combinations ignore order and permutations count it.
Neither requires repetition nor forbids finite sets; both use finite distinct objects.
Both are counting tools; neither is restricted to probabilities or events.
